messages:
maya: Quick RFC follow-up — we need to pick a scoping model for API keys/service auth. Per-project keys (edge enforced) vs per-service keys + broker (runtime delegation). Which direction do we take?

sam: Project-scoped wins on enforcement and tenant isolation. Ops likes it because edge can block cross-project calls easily. But downsides: key sprawl and not great for short-lived service-to-service flows.

chris: Leaning per-service + broker. Fewer long-lived secrets, rotate centrally, can mint ephemeral tokens with precise aud/claims. Con: needs runtime mapping and more infra.

olivia: If we do per-service we must have very clear audit + limits so one compromised service can't call everything. Could use aud claim like `aud: projects/1234/service/metrics` and RBAC check at the receiver.

maya: RBAC in every service is extra dev burden; ops prefers edge-level policy. But edge-only doesn't solve background jobs or internal scheduled tasks that legitimately call across projects.

auth-bot: :gear: keys-insights report ready — ~37k active API keys, 60% missing tags. Shows we have noise today. https://internal/keys/report

chris: Proposal: hybrid model — default project-scoped keys for humans/ingress; allow service-scoped ephemeral tokens minted by a broker for svc->svc calls. Broker enforces policy (who can mint for which target project/service).

olivia: Hybrid seems pragmatic. Questions: 1) How do services discover the broker? 2) Do we propagate original principal or replace with broker identity?

maya: Discovery via service registry + sidecar env var. For propagation: propagate the original principal as a signed claim header (e.g., `x-origin-actor`) and require mTLS + signature verification at the receiver to prevent spoofing.

sam: Async workflows complicate header propagation. For workers, broker should mint a token embedding `origin` + `origin_ttl` so the claim persists even when header can't. Keep these tokens short-lived.

chris: Implementation sketch:
```
POST /broker/token
body: { "service": "metrics", "target_project": "proj-123", "orig_token_id": "proj-456-key-abc" }
resp: { "token": "<jwt>", "ttl": 300, "aud": "proj-123:metrics" }
```
Broker logs orig_token_id for audit and links to request id.

olivia: Ops: revocation + introspection needed. Short TTLs help but we still need an introspection endpoint and a revocation list for immediate kill. Also consider pushing revocation events to edge caches.

maya: Fallback policy: if broker unavailable, deny cross-project minting by default. Edge continues to accept project-scoped calls as today.

sam: Agree. Next steps: quick RFC that defines hybrid broker pattern, minting API, claims (`aud`, `origin`, `origin_ttl`), revocation semantics, and audit logging. Volunteers?

chris: I'll draft the flow and sequence diagrams, include minimal schema for token claims. cc @olivia for ops constraints.

olivia: I'll write revocation/introspection requirements and add caching guidance for edge.

maya: I'll take threat model + header signing approach (how we sign `x-origin-actor`, key lifecycle). Let's sync tomorrow 11:00 for a 30m check.

sam: :thumbsup: Sounds good. If anyone sees obvious blockers (billing, quota, ratelimit mapping) call them out now so I can fold into the RFC.

chris: One potential blocker — rate-limit attribution: do we attribute usage to original project or to the service? Need to define so billing and quotas work.

maya: I'd prefer dual-attribution: primary billing to target project, billing metadata includes origin for traceability. We'll spec that.

olivia: Noted. I'll validate RPS quotas map cleanly to this model.

maya: Thanks all — will capture notes in the RFC template and link back here when draft is ready. :lock:
